staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the AddressSanitizer crash against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The saved line map matches `HTMLparser.c:2761` in `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` and the staged patch inserts the missing EOF guard immediately after `CUR_CHAR(l)` in the same function.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ at `HTMLparser.c:2761`. Source analysis shows that `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` calls the stateful helper `CUR_CHAR(l)` and then, without any EOF-state guard, unconditionally executes `NEXTL(l)` and re-enters the loop header. The saved ASan report proves that the loop-header dereference ultimately occurs at `"" + 1`, one byte past the global empty string, but the exact internal producer of the earlier EOF/sentinel state is not uniquely identified by the staged source evidence here.

bug_description.original: A use-of-uninitialized-value in htmlParseHTMLAttribute (HTMLparser.c) can cause an out-of-bounds read / global-buffer-overflow while parsing HTML attribute values. The parser may read past a local buffer into adjacent global memory, leading to crashes, incorrect behavior, or potential information disclosure.
bug_description.normalized: The staged OSS-Fuzz testcase is 16 bytes long. The fuzz harness consumes the first eight bytes as `opts` and `maxAlloc`, leaving the exact HTML payload `<h c=a\xFF ` for the reproduced pull-parser path. `htmlReadMemory()` materializes that payload into a parser context, `htmlParseContentInternal()` admits it as a start tag because it begins with `<h`, and `htmlParseAttribute()` reaches unquoted attribute parsing for `c=a\xFF `. In `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()`, the first loop iteration consumes ASCII `a` and advances to the next byte. On the second iteration `CUR_CHAR(l)` is called on attacker byte `0xFF`; `htmlCurrentChar()` reports invalid UTF-8 and may change parser state or input handling while returning control to the caller. Vulnerable `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` immediately continues without checking whether `ctxt->instate` became `XML_PARSER_EOF`, still uses `l` in `NEXTL(l)`, and then re-enters the loop header. The saved ASan report proves that the subsequent loop-header dereference reads at `"" + 1`, one byte past the global empty string defined in `parserInternals.c`, but the staged artifacts do not isolate which internal source-level operation first installed the EOF/sentinel state before that dereference. The staged patch adds exactly the missing `if (ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF) { xmlFree(buffer); return(NULL); }` guard after `CUR_CHAR(l)`.

source.description: First project-code consumption of the attacker-controlled HTML bytes on the reproduced pull-parser path. This statement materializes the fuzzed document fragment into the libxml2 parser context that later drives start-tag and attribute parsing.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 16 bytes: `20 20 20 20 68 74 69 30 3c 68 20 63 3d 61 ff 20`. The harness in `fuzz/html.c` consumes the first 8 bytes as `opts` and `maxAlloc`, so this call receives the exact document buffer `<h c=a\xFF ` (8 bytes) and the matching `size`.

sink.description: Crash sink. When control returns to this loop header after the unchecked post-`CUR_CHAR(l)` path, the saved AddressSanitizer report shows the `CUR` dereference reading at `"" + 1`, one byte past the global empty string.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. `CUR_CHAR(l)` is a stateful helper reached on the malformed attribute byte `0xFF`, but vulnerable code does not check whether the call left `ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF` before continuing to use `l` and re-enter the loop.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later attribute value bytes, including the exact malformed byte `0xFF`, enter project code here when the HTML payload `<h c=a\xFF ` is wrapped in a parser context.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific parser gate. The admitted document payload begins with `<h`, so this branch recognizes the input as an HTML start tag and continues into element parsing rather than comments, PI handling, or plain character data.

coarse_trace.summary: The pull parser materializes the attacker-controlled HTML bytes and admits the witness as a start tag because the document buffer starts with `<h`.
Start-tag parsing reaches attribute `c=a\xFF `, selects the unquoted attribute-value parser, and consumes ASCII `a` in the first loop iteration.
On the second iteration, `CUR_CHAR(l)` processes attacker byte `0xFF`, may change parser state during encoding handling, and the patch's missing EOF guard becomes load-bearing.

Vulnerable code still executes `NEXTL(l)` with `l` from `CUR_CHAR(l)` and, on the crashing execution evidenced by ASan, advances past the empty sentinel string before the next loop-header `CUR` read triggers the saved global-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. The pull parser materializes the exact attacker-controlled HTML fragment `<h c=a\xFF ` into the parser context used on the reproduced crash path.
The document buffer begins with `<h`, so this branch admits the sample as an HTML start tag and routes parsing into `htmlParseElementInternal()`.
After tag name `h`, start-tag parsing stays in the attribute loop because the next bytes are ` c=a\xFF `, not tag terminators and not EOF.
After parsing attacker-controlled attribute name `c` and the `=` delimiter, the parser hands the attribute value bytes `a\xFF ` to the attribute-value parser.
Because the attacker value begins with unquoted `a` rather than `'` or `"`, HTML parsing takes the unquoted-value path with `stop == 0`.
The unquoted attribute-value loop starts on ASCII `a`: the current byte is nonzero and, with `stop == 0`, not yet terminated by whitespace or `>`.
First loop iteration: `CUR_CHAR(l)` reads the current attacker byte `a` with `l == 1`, so the parser treats it as a normal single-byte attribute character.
The first iteration advances the parser cursor by `l == 1`, moving from `a` to the next attacker-controlled byte `0xFF` while keeping the attribute-value loop active.

Root cause. On the second iteration `CUR_CHAR(l)` processes attacker byte `0xFF`. In `htmlCurrentChar()`, this byte takes the invalid-UTF-8 path, reports an encoding error, and may change parser state or input handling before returning control with `l` set for the current byte. Vulnerable code does not check whether that helper also left `ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF`; the staged patch adds exactly that missing guard here.

No EOF check intervenes after `CUR_CHAR(l)`, so the function still applies `NEXTL(l)` using the length produced for the malformed byte even if the parser has transitioned to EOF. The staged patch shows this unchecked advance is the missing obligation; the staged artifacts do not isolate which internal source-level operation first produced any EOF/sentinel cursor state seen later at the sink.

Sink. The saved ASan report shows this loop-header dereference reads at address `"" + 1`, immediately after the empty global string in `parserInternals.c`, which is the observed global-buffer-overflow READ.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with the reconstructed root cause because it inserts an EOF-state guard immediately after `CUR_CHAR(l)` in `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build and therefore does not claim dynamic confirmation.

format.name: OSS-Fuzz html testcase buffer
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 16-byte witness. Its first 8 bytes are consumed by the fuzz harness as `opts` and `maxAlloc`; the remaining 8-byte HTML payload is exactly `<h c=a\xFF `. The load-bearing property is the unquoted attribute value `a\xFF ` inside that fragment: the first byte `a` keeps `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` in its normal loop, and the exact following byte `0xFF` is the malformed character that reaches the missing post-`CUR_CHAR(l)` EOF check fixed by the patch.
